_note: Evals use bundled synthetic fixtures (see files/make_fixtures.py and files/make_extra_fixtures.py) rather than nilearn.datasets fetchers, because Anthropic's sandbox blocks the CDN hosts the fetchers download from. End users with normal internet should use the built-in fetchers — the skill recommends them by default.

evals.name: glm_first_level_block_design
evals.prompt: I have a small task-fMRI dataset and I want to fit a first-level GLM. The BOLD file is at evals/files/glm/bold.nii.gz with TR=7s, the events are in evals/files/glm/events.tsv (a single trial type called 'active' in a block design), and there's a brain mask at evals/files/glm/brain_mask.nii.gz. Please fit the model, compute the contrast for 'active' vs baseline, save the z-map and a glass-brain visualization to ./results_glm/, and tell me what z-range you saw. Also generate an HTML report.
evals.expected_output: A working FirstLevelModel fit on the provided fixture, with t_r=7 set explicitly, the 'active' contrast computed and saved as a NIfTI, glass-brain PNG saved, HTML report saved, and a written summary that includes the actual z-range observed.
expectations: Reads bold.nii.gz from evals/files/glm/ (does not invent a different path or call a nilearn dataset fetcher)
Loads events.tsv as a DataFrame with onset, duration, trial_type columns
Instantiates FirstLevelModel with t_r=7.0 (or 7) explicitly
Calls .fit() on the model with the bold image and events
Calls .compute_contrast('active', ...) (or equivalent) and gets a z-map
Saves at least one .nii.gz file to ./results_glm/
Saves at least one .png file (e.g., glass brain or stat map) to ./results_glm/
Generates an HTML report (e.g., via make_glm_report)
Reports the actual z-range in the response text (not a placeholder)
Uses standardize=False (or omits it; the default is False for FirstLevelModel) and not the deprecated 'True' value for any maskers used

evals.name: connectivity_three_subjects_correlation
evals.prompt: I have 3 subjects of resting-state fMRI in evals/files/connectivity/ — files are sub-01_bold.nii.gz, sub-02_bold.nii.gz, sub-03_bold.nii.gz with TR=2s and matching sub-XX_confounds.tsv files. There's a 6-region label atlas at evals/files/connectivity/atlas.nii.gz with names in atlas_labels.csv. Extract timeseries for each subject (use the confounds), compute correlation matrices, and give me a mean matrix heatmap plus a glass-brain connectome. Output to ./connectivity_out/.
evals.expected_output: Three-subject correlation pipeline: NiftiLabelsMasker built from atlas.nii.gz with t_r=2 and bandpass filter set, timeseries extracted for each subject with their matching confounds, a correlation matrix per subject, a mean matrix, a heatmap PNG, and a connectome glass-brain PNG.
expectations: Uses NiftiLabelsMasker (not NiftiMapsMasker — atlas is deterministic labels)
Constructs masker with t_r=2.0 explicitly
Constructs masker with standardize='zscore_sample' (the string, not deprecated True)
Sets low_pass and high_pass on the masker (or filters before extraction)
Loads each subject's matching confounds TSV and passes to fit_transform
Uses ConnectivityMeasure with kind='correlation'
Produces 3 timeseries arrays of shape (150, 6) (or fit_transform on a list)
Computes a per-subject and a mean connectivity matrix
Saves a matrix heatmap PNG to ./connectivity_out/
Saves a glass-brain connectome PNG using plot_connectome with coords
Mean matrix shows strong positive correlation between regions 1-2 and 3-4, negative between 5-6 (the known structure in the fixture)

evals.name: decoding_face_vs_house_leave_one_run_out
evals.prompt: Run an MVPA decoding analysis: the 4D BOLD is at evals/files/decoding/bold.nii.gz where each volume is one trial (TR=2s). Labels and run numbers are in evals/files/decoding/labels.csv (columns 'labels' with 'face'/'house', 'chunks' with run number 0-5). Use the VT mask at evals/files/decoding/vt_mask.nii.gz, SVC classifier, and leave-one-run-out cross-validation. Tell me the mean accuracy across folds and how it compares to chance. Save the weight map as a NIfTI and a plot to ./decoder_out/.
evals.expected_output: Decoder pipeline with SVC, LeaveOneGroupOut CV on the run variable, fit on the VT mask, accuracy reported with chance level (0.5), weight map saved as NIfTI and PNG.
expectations: Loads labels.csv and uses the 'labels' column as y and 'chunks' as groups
Uses nilearn.decoding.Decoder (not raw sklearn) with estimator='svc'
Uses LeaveOneGroupOut from sklearn.model_selection (or equivalent group CV)
Passes groups=chunks to decoder.fit()
Uses the vt_mask.nii.gz as the mask= argument (not whole brain)
Uses standardize='zscore_sample' (not deprecated True)
Reports mean accuracy in the response text
Reports the chance level (0.5 for binary) in the response text
Saves the weight map as a .nii.gz in ./decoder_out/
Saves a plot of the weight map as PNG in ./decoder_out/

evals.name: glm_statistical_thresholding_fdr
evals.prompt: I've already decided to use the GLM fixture from evals/files/glm/: bold.nii.gz (TR=7s), events.tsv (trial type 'active'), and brain_mask.nii.gz. Fit a first-level GLM, compute the 'active' contrast z-map, then apply FDR thresholding at alpha=0.05 using nilearn.glm.threshold_stats_img. Report the FDR threshold value, how many voxels survive, and the peak z-score in the surviving map. Save both the unthresholded and thresholded z-maps as NIfTIs, plus a side-by-side visualization showing unthresholded vs FDR-corrected, to ./results_threshold/.
evals.expected_output: GLM fit → contrast → threshold_stats_img with height_control='fdr', alpha=0.05. Reports the numeric FDR threshold, surviving voxel count, and peak z-score. Saves unthresholded z-map, thresholded z-map, and a comparison PNG.
expectations: Calls nilearn.glm.threshold_stats_img (not just plot_stat_map threshold argument)
Passes height_control='fdr' and alpha=0.05 explicitly
Reports the actual numeric FDR threshold value in the response text
Reports the number of voxels surviving the threshold
Reports the peak z-score in the surviving map
Saves the unthresholded z-map as a .nii.gz in ./results_threshold/
Saves the thresholded z-map as a .nii.gz in ./results_threshold/
Saves at least one PNG visualization to ./results_threshold/
Does not confuse the plot_stat_map threshold argument with statistical inference

evals.name: second_level_group_glm
evals.prompt: I have first-level z-maps from 8 subjects: evals/files/second_level/sub-01_zmap.nii.gz through sub-08_zmap.nii.gz, and a brain mask at evals/files/second_level/brain_mask.nii.gz. Run a second-level (group) GLM to test for a population-level activation (one-sample t-test against zero). Use an intercept-only design matrix. Compute the second-level z-map, apply FDR correction at alpha=0.05, and report where the group activates. Save the group z-map and a glass-brain plot to ./results_group/.
evals.expected_output: SecondLevelModel fit on 8 z-maps with intercept design, contrast computed, FDR thresholding applied, group z-map and glass-brain saved to ./results_group/. Response includes numeric description of where group activation is found.
expectations: Uses nilearn.glm.second_level.SecondLevelModel (not FirstLevelModel)
Builds design matrix with pandas DataFrame containing a single 'intercept' column of ones, length 8
Calls second_level_model.fit(zmaps_list, design_matrix=...)
Calls .compute_contrast() to get the group z-map
Applies threshold_stats_img with height_control='fdr', alpha=0.05
Saves group z-map as .nii.gz in ./results_group/
Saves a glass-brain PNG in ./results_group/
Reports the location or extent of group-level activation in the response

evals.name: seed_based_connectivity
evals.prompt: I have one subject's resting-state BOLD at evals/files/connectivity/sub-01_bold.nii.gz (TR=2s) and confounds at evals/files/connectivity/sub-01_confounds.tsv. Run a seed-based connectivity analysis: use a 6mm-radius sphere centered at MNI (-16, -16, 0) as the seed ROI (this is region_1 in the atlas). Extract the seed timeseries with NiftiSpheresMasker, extract whole-brain voxel timeseries with NiftiMasker (using the atlas as mask — or the brain implicitly), regress out confounds for both, then compute the correlation between the seed timeseries and every brain voxel. Save the seed correlation map as a NIfTI and a glass-brain plot to ./seed_out/. Report the peak correlation value.
evals.expected_output: NiftiSpheresMasker seed extraction + NiftiMasker whole-brain extraction, correlation computed, seed-map saved as NIfTI and plotted. Peak correlation reported.
expectations: Uses NiftiSpheresMasker with seeds=[(-16, -16, 0)] and radius=6 (or nearby value)
Passes t_r=2.0 to NiftiSpheresMasker
Uses standardize='zscore_sample' (not deprecated True) for both maskers
Passes confounds to fit_transform for both maskers
Computes voxel-wise correlation between seed timeseries and brain timeseries (e.g. np.corrcoef or stats.pearsonr)
Builds a NIfTI image from the correlation array using the masker's inverse_transform or nibabel directly
Saves seed correlation map as .nii.gz in ./seed_out/
Saves a glass-brain PNG in ./seed_out/
Reports the peak (maximum) correlation value in the response

evals.name: niftimasker_signal_extraction_tsnr
evals.prompt: Use evals/files/glm/bold.nii.gz (TR=7s) and evals/files/glm/brain_mask.nii.gz to extract a whole-brain timeseries matrix with NiftiMasker. Apply detrending and high-pass filtering (cutoff 0.01 Hz) but do NOT standardize (we want raw signal units for tSNR). After extraction, compute the temporal SNR map: for each voxel, tSNR = mean(timeseries) / std(timeseries). Report the median tSNR across voxels and save the tSNR map as a NIfTI and a stat-map PNG to ./tsnr_out/.
evals.expected_output: NiftiMasker extraction with detrend=True, high_pass=0.01, t_r=7, standardize=False. tSNR computed per voxel as mean/std. Median tSNR reported. tSNR NIfTI and PNG saved.
expectations: Uses NiftiMasker with mask_img pointing to brain_mask.nii.gz
Sets t_r=7.0 on the masker
Sets detrend=True on the masker
Sets high_pass=0.01 on the masker
Sets standardize=False (we want raw signal, not z-scores)
Extracted timeseries has shape (96, n_voxels) — 96 timepoints
Computes tSNR = mean(axis=0) / std(axis=0) per voxel
Reports the median tSNR value in the response text
Converts tSNR array back to a NIfTI image using masker.inverse_transform
Saves tSNR NIfTI to ./tsnr_out/
Saves a stat-map or brain-map PNG to ./tsnr_out/

evals.name: multirun_first_level_glm
evals.prompt: I have two runs of task fMRI: evals/files/multirun/run-01_bold.nii.gz and run-02_bold.nii.gz (TR=7s, 48 volumes each), with matching events in run-01_events.tsv and run-02_events.tsv (trial type 'active', same block design in each run), and a brain mask at evals/files/multirun/brain_mask.nii.gz. Fit a single FirstLevelModel across both runs (pass both BOLD files and both event DataFrames as lists), compute the 'active' contrast, and compare the z-map peak to what you'd get from run-01 alone. Save z-maps and glass-brain plots for the combined model and run-01-only model to ./multirun_out/. Report both peak z-scores.
evals.expected_output: FirstLevelModel fit with a list of two BOLD images and a list of two events DataFrames, contrast computed from combined model, comparison with single-run model. Both peak z-scores reported, z-maps and plots saved.
expectations: Passes a list of two NIfTI images to FirstLevelModel.fit(), not a single concatenated image
Passes a list of two events DataFrames (one per run) to .fit()
Sets t_r=7.0 explicitly
Fits a second model on run-01 alone for comparison
Calls .compute_contrast('active') on both models
Reports peak z-score for the combined model in the response text
Reports peak z-score for the single-run model in the response text
Combined model peak z-score should be >= single-run peak (more data = more power)
Saves z-maps as .nii.gz in ./multirun_out/
Saves glass-brain PNGs to ./multirun_out/
